title: DataFrame.merge with empty frame and Int64 column gives object dtype

labels.name: ExtensionArray
labels.description: Extending pandas with custom dtypes or arrays.

body:
#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example if possible

```python
x = pd.DataFrame({
    'date': pd.Series([pd.Timestamp('2018-01-01')]),
    'value': pd.Series([1], dtype='Int64')
})
y = x[:0]
z = x.merge(y, on='date', how='left')

# z
        date  value_x value_y
0 2018-01-01        1     NaN

# z.dtypes

date       datetime64[ns]
value_x             Int64
value_y            object
dtype: object
```
#### Problem descriptioy

The dtype of the `value_y` column should be `Int64`. 

#### Expected Output

```python
date       datetime64[ns]
value_x             Int64
value_y             Int64
dtype: object
```

comments_details.body:
@josham : Given that you have a `NaN` in `value_y`, it would be impossible to have `Int64` (would be a floating dtype actually).  That being said, uncertain as to why you're getting `object` though...

cc @jreback
I agree that this should be able to return Int types here; this was just put in place in 0.24 so may not be well handled for empty types

@jreback I came across another merge issue with Int64. I can add to this issue or create another, let me know what you prefer.

```python
x = pd.DataFrame({
    'date': [pd.Timestamp('2018-01-01')],
    'value': pd.Series([np.nan], dtype='Int64')
})
y = pd.DataFrame({
    'date': [pd.Timestamp('2018-01-01')],
    'value': pd.Series([4], dtype='Int64')
})
z = x.merge(y, on=['date'])
```

@jreback, @TomAugspurger the following seems to fix both issues. Does this seem correct to you?

```
--- a/pandas/core/internals/concat.py
+++ b/pandas/core/internals/concat.py
@@ -190,6 +190,8 @@ class JoinUnit(object):
                     pass
                 elif getattr(self.block, 'is_sparse', False):
                     pass
+                elif getattr(self.block, 'is_extension', False):
+                    pass
                 else:
                     missing_arr = np.empty(self.shape, dtype=empty_dtype)
                     missing_arr.fill(fill_value)
```
